Title: Updating Network Software License
Content: To update existing Software License Key due to renewing license or adding copies, please follow the instruction below. 1. Generate C2V file with the RUS executable file, located at the bottom of this post, and submit your C2V file through this page (Logging in with your Company ID is required). Make sure the number in the red box has been changed correctly.

Title: Guide for Installing Network Offline Version on the Internet Environment
Content: Guide for Installing Network Version on the Internet Environment Objective Set up Marvelous Designer/Marvelous Designer Network Version on the Internet environment. Note that you do not need to follow the set-up guidelines below when a Server PC and Client PC are under the same local network environment. Simply plugging the dongle key into a Server PC enables you to run Marvelous Designer or Marvelous Designer on any PCs under the same local network as the Server PC located without any extra settings. 1.) Set-up on Server PC Operation 1. Plug the dongle key in the Server PC and install the HASP Driver. HASP Driver gets automatically installed during the software installation. However if any trouble occurs during the process or in case of Server only being connected with the dongle key, HASP Driver should be installed manually. Guideline for Sentinel HASP Driver Manual Installation 2. Make sure Port 1947 is open in the firewall. Port 1947 should be automatically opened once the HASP Driver gets installed however, occasionally it fails to open the port in certain PCs. In this case, go to the firewall settings and open the port manually. Port 1947 is being used for communication between the Client PC and dongle key in the Server PC in order to get an authentication. Setting methods varies considerably in the types of firewall, therefore please ask for support from your network manager. 3. Make sure the local IP address of the Server is static. (Local IP is dynamically allocated Intranet IP by the router.) The local IP address gets changed when the router is restarted if the local IP is not set in static status. To avoid repetitive IP reset in the process, 'port forwarding', set your Server's local IP as 'static'. 4. Port-forward Port 1947 for TCP and UDP of the Server's local IP in the router setting. Port-forwarding enables to transmit the data from Client/Server to Server/Client through Port 1947. Port-forwarding method vary considerably in the types of router therefore please ask for support from your network manager. Note: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_forwarding http://www.wikihow.com/Set-up-Port-Forwarding-on-a-Router 2.) Set-up on Client PC Operation 1. Run Marvelous Designer/Marvelous Designer Network Version installer. 2. Make sure Port 1947 is open in the firewall. Port 1947 should automatically be opened once the HASP Driver gets installed however, occasionally it fails to open the port in certain PCs. In this case, go to the firewall settings and open the port manually. Port 1947 is being used for communication between the Client PC and the dongle key in the Server PC in order to get an authentication. Setting methods varies considerably in the types of firewall, therefore please ask for support from your network manager. 3. Set external IP of the Server on the dongle key configuration to let the software reaches the Server for an authentication. This can be done through Sentinel Admin Control Center which is automatically installed during the HASP Driver installation. Access to http://localhost:1947 Click on 'Configuration' (the red box) 4. Click on the third tab, which is called, 'Access to Remote License Managers'. 5. Make sure to check on 'Aggressive Search for Remote License' and to type the Server PC's external IP in 'Specify Search Parameters' (note that the external IP is different from the local IP mentioned in the 'Set-up on Server PC'). You are able to see the external IP of the Server PC on the website (http://www.whatismyip.com/).

Title: Mac - Certificate Authentication Issues After Installation
Content: Objective How to solve certificate authentication issues after installation in Mac. Operation OPTION 1 Note: Please make sure to download both certificate files from the links below to allow the program to run properly. Click on the link to download the Certificate_1(certificate.crt) /Certificate_2(IntermediateCA.crt) file. Navigate to the folder where the Certificate file was downloaded. Double-click the Certificate file, then click Add. Keychain Access window appears. Double-click on the Certificate file in the Keychain Access window. The certificate information appears, then click on Trust to expand its menu. Under "When using this certificate" set it to Always Trust from the drop-down menu. Restart the computer. Start the program. OPTION 2 Note: Should OPTION 1 fail to solve the issue, please use OPTION 2. Click on the link to download the Certificate_1(certificate.crt) / Certificate_2(IntermediateCA.crt)/ Certificate_3(china-certificate.crt) file. Run Terminal.app. Enter "cd" then locate the folder where the file was downloaded in Finder, and drag and drop into Terminal.app. Note: Possible Errors Confirm if there is a space after cd. Confirm that the file path to where the downloaded file is located is correct. Press Enter on the keyboard, input "ls-al" then press Enter on the keyboard again. Input sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k/Library/Keychains/System.keychain certificate.crt sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k/Library/Keychains/System.keychain IntermediateCA.crt sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k/Library/Keychains/System.keychain china-certificate.crt then press Enter on the keyboard. Enter the password associated with the Mac account, then start the program.

Title: System Requirements (June 2024)
Content: Applicable for: All users of Marvelous Designer software In this document, Marvelous Designer or Marvelous Designer software refers only to the Marvelous Designer software installed on the user's local computer and does not refer to CLO-SET and various other CLO products. Windows Category Minimum Recommended (Best Build) OS Windows 10 64-bit ( 1903 or later) Windows 10 64-bit (22H2 or later) 1) 2) 3) Windows 11 64-bit (23H2 or later) Processor AMD Ryzen 5 1500X Intel Core-i5 6400 AMD Ryzen 7/9 7000 series or higher Intel Core-i7/i9 14th Gen or higher Memory 8GB 32GB or more 4) Graphics card NVIDIA GeForce GTX 960 or NVIDIA Quadro P2200 NVIDIA GeForce RTX series or NVIDIA Quadro RTX , RTX A series 5) 6) 7) Storage HDD 10GB or more SSD 20GB or more Screen 1920x1080(HD) 2560x1440(QHD), 3840x2160(4K) Input device 3-button mouse 3-button mouse Network Internet connection required Internet connection required Windows - Read more 1) Windows updates and patches are highly recommended. Windows Update - Microsoft Support 2) If dll-related errors occur while installing or running Marvelous Designer, install the latest Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable. X64 architecture is recommended. Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable latest supported downloads 3) Marvelous Designer software cannot run on Windows 10/11 N which media features removed. Download and install the Media Feature Pack from the Microsoft website. Media Feature Pack for Windows 10/11 N (February 2023) 4) For smoother operation, 16GB or more of memory is recommended. 32GB or more of memory is recommended if you are using multiple software at the same time and/or dealing with huge and complex garments. 5) Marvelous Designer utilizes Nvidia CUDA acceleration technology for Marvelous Designer GPU-Simulation. So computers with only Intel Graphics or AMD graphics cards do not benefit from GPU acceleration that speeds up Marvelous Designer simulation. 6) For graphics card-related issues, please see the following guide. In particular, please update your graphics card driver to the latest. Graphics Card Problems and Troubleshooting 7) Some mobile GPU processors from AMD and Intel may not fully support openGL, which is essential for running Marvelous Designer, and may not run Marvelous Designer. If you are using a laptop or graphics card with a built-in CPU, check with the hardware manufacturer for the GPU model and whether it supports openGL. Mac Category Minimum Recommended (Best Build) Mac models All Macs released after 2015 1) Intel-chip Macs released after 2018 2) Apple Silicon Macs: M1, M2, M3 macOS Monterey 12 *For macOS dependencies, check out the notes below 3) Ventura 13, Sonoma 14 Processor Intel Core-i5 4cores Apple Silicon 4) Memory 8GB 24GB or more Storage HDD 10GB or more SSD 20GB or more Screen 1280x800 Retina 4K, Retina 5K supported 5) Input devices 3-button mouse 3-button mouse Network Internet connection required Internet connection required Mac - Read more 1) Starting with Marvelous Designer v2024, the minimum macOS has been changed to Monterey 12. See which Macs are compatible with macOS Monterey 12 here. macOS Monterey is compatible with these computers 2) All Intel-chip macs do not have Nvidia graphics cards, so mac users cannot get the GPU-acceleration which is supported by Marvelous Designer software, but simulation is supported normally. 3) macOS dependencies Sierra 10.12: users can install and run up to Marvelous Designer 9. High Sierra 10.13: users can install and run up to Marvelous Designer 10. Mojave 10.14: users can install and run up to Marvelous Designer 10. Catalina 10.15: users can install and run up to Marvelous Designer 12.2. Please note that Marvelous Designer 11 and future versions will not run on macOS Mojave or earlier. 4) As of Marvelous Designer 11, provides a compatible build for both Apple Silicon macs and Intel-chip macs. If you want to use version 10 or lower on Apple Silicon Mac, you need to install Apple Rosetta. Visit here for more info. If you need to install Rosetta on your Mac - Apple Support 5) Marvelous Designer software supports Retina 5K and higher resolutions. However, it may run a bit slower in a resolution environment of 5K or higher. This is a known issue and is being improved. See also Marvelous Designer software does not support BootCamp in macOS. Marvelous Designer software can be installed and run in virtual server environments such as Virtual Machine and Virtual Desktop Infrastructure and in cloud services. However, in this case, the Marvelous Designer team does not provide technical support. Marvelous Designer software does not support Apple iOS, iPad OS, tvOS, Android OS, Windows Mobile, and Linux. Marvelous Designer software does not support 32-bit OS (e.g. Windows 7 32-bit) Marvelous Designer software can be downloaded as .exe or .dmg file format. It is not distributed in .msi or .pkg file format.

Title: Windows - Certificate Authentication Issues After Installation
Content: Objective How to resolve certificate authentication issues after installation in Windows. Operation OPTION1 Note: Please make sure to download both certificate files from the links below to allow the program to run properly. The certification files are attached at the bottom of the page. Click on the link to download the Certificate_1(certificate.crt) / Certificate_2(IntermediateCA.crt) file. Navigate to the folder where the Certificate file was downloaded. Right-click on the Certificate file, then click on Install Certificate. Certificate.crt IntermediateCA.crt Select Local Machine, then click Next. Select Place all certificates in the following store then click Browse... Click on Show physical stores at the bottom of the window. Expand the Trusted Root Certification Authorities folder. Click on Registry, then click OK. Click Next. Review the information, then click Finish. The import was successful message appears, then click OK. Start the program. OPTION 2 Note: Should OPTION 1 fail to solve the issue, please use OPTION 2. Download the Certificate_1 (certificate.crt) / Certificate_2 (IntermediateCA.crt)/ Certificate_3(china-certificate.crt) file attached below. Click on the Start button, then run CMD. In the command prompt, input cd location of the downloaded certificate file, then press Enter on the keyboard. Note: Path Cannot be Located Issue Confirm if there is a space after cd Confirm that the file path to where the downloaded file is located is correct. In the command prompt, input "certutil -addstore -user -f root certificate.crt" / "certutil -addstore -user -f root IntermediateCA.crt"/ "certutil -addstore -user -f root china-certificate.crt" then press Enter on the keyboard. Start the program again.

Title: Attach Pin to/Detach Pin from Avatar
Content: Objective Affix specific parts of the Garments to the Avatar. This function is commonly used for Simulation or recording animation for avoiding the Garment sliding off from the Avatar. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move or Select Mesh (Box) or Pin (Box) Operation Attach Pin to Avatar Create a pin to attach to an Avatar. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move or Select Mesh (Box) or Pin (Box) Right-click on the created pin select Attach Pin to Avatar/Attach All Pins to Avatar. The selected pin is now being attached to the nearest part of the Avatar. Note: Pins attached to the Avatar are unable to be selected or moved. Detach Pin from Avatar Right-click on the pin attached to the avatar select Detach from Avatar/Detach All Pins from Avatar. The attached pin is now being detached from the Avatar.

Title: Delete Pin
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary pins. Location Main Menu Edit Context Menu 3D Garment Delete All Pins / Delete All Pins on Selected Patterns Pin Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Delete Selected Pin / Delete All Pins Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Edit Context Menu 3D Garment Delete All Pins / Delete All Pins on Selected Patterns Pin Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Delete Selected Pin / Delete All Pins The selected pin is now being deleted. Note: Selecting a created pin while holding W key on keyboard also deletes the pin.

Title: Create Pin
Content: Objective Affix specific portions of the Garment and utilize Pin similar to the Freeze function. It is also convenient when turning/flipping over collars, lapels, or cuffs. Location Pin Tool Main Menu 3D Garment Pin (Box) / Pin (Lasso) 3D Toolbar (Click for more than 2 seconds) Pin (Box) / Pin (Lasso) Select/Move Tool Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move 3D Toolbar Select/Move Operation Pin Tool Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Pin (Box) / Pin (Lasso) 3D Toolbar (Click more than 2 seconds) Pin (Box) / Pin (Lasso) The Garment mesh is now displayed in red in both the 3D and 2D windows. Click on a vertex (a point of the mesh). A Pin is created on the selected point. Or click on a desired area on the Garment Click and drag to select the area. Pins are created on the vertex of the selected area. Pins can also be created on 2D Patterns. Click and drag, or use the Gizmo to move the pinned mesh as desired in the 3D window. Note: Click and drag on the 2D Pattern while pressing Shift+Ctrl on the keyboard to create additional pinned areas. Adversely, click and drag on the 2D Pattern while pressing Ctrl on the keyboard to remove Pins from existing pinned areas. Select/Move Tool Click on the Select/Move tool in the 3D window. Click while pressing W on the keyboard to create a Pin on a specific point. A Pin is created on the selected point. If the input language is set to Korean, a Pin cannot be created when pressing W on the keyboard. Make sure to change the input language to English. Note: Create Pin on Segment Double-click on a Pattern outline in either the 3D or 2D window to create Pins on a segment. When creating Pins on the Pattern in the 2D window, Pins are generated on adjacent segment vertices when the angle difference is less than 20. Create Pin on Pattern Double-click on a Pattern in either the 3D or 2D window to create Pins on a Pattern. Create Pin on Internal Line (ver4.0.0) Use the same procedure as above to create Pins on specific Internal Lines and Shapes.

Title: Select Mesh (Above Ver. 2024.0)
Content: Select a portion of or the full pattern mesh for a 3D garment. Select Mesh Steps 1. Select a tool from the path below. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Select Mesh (Brush) / (Box) / (Lasso) 3D Window Toolbar Select Mesh (Brush) / (Box) / (Lasso) 2. Select an area in the 3D Garment. Brush Dialog Options Menu Description Strength Sets the strength of the brush's area selection. Size Sets the size of the brush. * You can use the [ ] keyboard shortcut to resize the brush. Focal Sets the size of the brush's center area. The center area is the area where 100% of the set intensity is applied. Add/delete parts of the selected area Shift key: Selects the existing selection with a toggle. Shift+Ctrl keys: The area is added unconditionally. Ctrl key: The region is unconditionally deleted. Line/Pattern Selection Double-clicking on a Pattern Outline/Inner Line segment selects the line segment, and double-clicking on a Vertex (point on the mesh) inside the pattern selects the pattern unit. End Result The mesh is selected for the area. Mesh Options You can apply Subdivide, Freeze, Solidify, Strengthen, and more to the selected mesh. The following menu of mesh options is available by right-clicking on the selected mesh. Menu Description Subdivide The selection will be divided according to the properties set. Create Pin Creates pins at the vertices of the area. Roll Up Horizontally Rolls up (flips) the selection in a horizontal direction. Roll Up Vertically Rolls up (flips) the selection in a vertical direction. Freeze Freezes the selected area. Solidify Solidify the selected area in shape. Strengthen (ver. 2024.0) Allows you to set Strengthen settings for the selected area. Export to USD Layer Exports as a USD layer. The selected options will be applied to the area, and the color of each area will indicate whether it is Subdivide, Pin, Freeze, Keep Shape, or Enhance. Subdivision Properties Set the properties of the applied options in the properties window. Menu Description Name Sets the name of the subdivision region. Level Sets the number of division steps. You can enter a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 3. Smooth Steps the mesh between the subdivision region and the outer region. Solidify/ Strengthen Properties Menu Description Strength Sets the strength of the stiffness. Delete individual/all Mesh Options Select the items with the option applied and press the Delete key on the keyboard to delete them. Right-clicking on an item with the option applied allows you to delete the selected mesh options individually and globally. Right-clicking on an optioned pattern allows you to delete all mesh options individually. Selecting all mesh options Right-clicking on an item with the option applied makes a full selection menu of the selected options available. Right-click on a pattern with an option applied to it to enable full selection by mesh option. Showing/Hide Mesh Options Show Subdivision The created subdivisions can be viewed and turned off from the View 3D Garment Show Subdivisions menu. Note: Right-click to open the 3D Background Options Menu Show/Hide Color (Show/Hide 3D Color Ver. 2024.1) to hide the Subdivide, Freeze, or solidify color display in the 3D window.

Title: Account Manual
Content: Company ID - End User ID Relationship diagram Difference between End User and Company ID Company ID: Your "Company ID" is an administrator account that can manage "End User IDs" owned by the license manager or purchaser. Through your Team Console page on our website, you can create, delete and change the password of any "End User ID" that belongs to the "Company ID". Purchasing and assigning a license to an "End User ID" are authorities only available to a Company ID. A Company ID cannot contain any type of license on its own and therefore cannot be used to log into the software. End User ID: An "End User ID" is an account for actual users which can hold licenses and is used to log in to the software. An "End User ID" cannot be used to purchase a license through our website. An End User ID can only be used to modify some of the information on its account page (i.e. Name, Country, Territory, Region, or Profile Photo) License Purchase Team Console Access Store Item Purchase Log In To Software Company ID O O O X End User ID X X X O * Note In the case of Enterprise Users who have created their IDs before the deployment of the Company ID - End User ID structure, you would already have the Company ID designated by us. In order for you to find your Company ID, please contact us at support@marvelousdesigner.com Personal ID Guideline Personal ID: A Personal ID is an account for all personal license users. Personal ID can only purchase personal licenses. How to use My Account Dashboard In the Dashboard section, you can view the general information of your account, as well as the licenses you possess at the moment *License Users can view all licenses they have access to. They can also download different update installers under each license version in the archive list. Account On the Account section, you can check more specific information of the account, as well as modify some of the information including Name, Profile photo, Occupation, Billing Address, Country/ Territory/ Region. *Newsletter Subscription Users can either turn on and off the newsletter subscription option with this slide bar **Delete Account Users can proceed to delete their account as long as there is no active license existing at the moment License On the License section, you can check the Name of the product you have/ Expiry date of it/ Different versions of installers on Windows and Mac OS, Cancellation *Order History Users can check on your order history that includes order date, product, payment method, amount, invoice **Cancel This section shows a button for users to cancel their subscription, but for those of who have purchased a license in prepaid method or possess perpetual version will have blank in a section instead

Title: Puckering (ver.2024.0)
Content: Create puckering You can create puckering on pattern outlines, inner line segments, and sewing lines. Steps Segment puckering Select a line segment to create puckering. 1. Select the Segment Puckering tool via the path below. Location Main Menu Materials Puckering Segment Puckering 2D Window Toolbar Segment Puckering 2. Click the segment you want to create a puckering for. Free puckering You can create puckering on pattern outlines and internal lines regardless of segment points. 1. Select the Free Puckering tool via the path below. Location Main Menu Materials Puckering Free Puckering 2D Window Toolbar Free Puckering 2. Set the first and last points on the line where you want to create the puckering by clicking the mouse. Seamline puckering You can create a puckering on a pattern seamline. 1. Select the Seamline Puckering tool via the path below. Location Main Menu Materials Puckering Seamline Puckering 2D Window Toolbar Seamline Puckering 2. Click on the Sewing Line to create the puckering. End Result Puckering is created on that line. You can see the created puckering on the 3D Garment. For Seamline Puckering, the puckering will appear on one or both Sewing Lines depending on the 'Placement' set in the Puckering Properties. Note: In the 2D window, you can create puckering in one step by clicking and dragging an area to include all the desired line segments. Puckering cannot be created twice. Edit Puckering You can select and modify the puckering applied (move the position, modify the length / width). Steps 1. Select the Edit Puckering tool via the path below. Location Main Menu Materials Puckering Edit Puckering 2D Window Toolbar Edit Puckering 2. Click &amp drag the line segment or point to edit the puckering. 3. To delete the puckering, select the puckering line and press the Delete key on the keyboard. End Result Move Position: Select &amp drag the puckering line to move the entire line. Modify Length: Click and drag the end point of the puckering to modify the length. If you right-click while editing the length, a Moving Distance dialogue will appear, allowing you to move it to the desired numerical value. Puckering object properties and options Set the properties of a puckering objects. Steps 1. Select a puckering object with the Edit Puckering tool. The Properties displays on the property window of the selected puckering. Puckering object properties Property Description Name Change the name of the puckering object. Style Change the puckering style. Extend Extends the start/end of the puckering to the outline of the 2D pattern. Offset Offset Adjusts the distance the puckering is spaced from the pattern outline. Include or exclude the width of the puckering from the spacing as needed. Z Offset Adjust the Z-axis distance of the puckering. Placement Puckering Select where to apply the puckering on either side of the Seamline puckering. Flip Only available when you select a puckering applied on an internal line. Toggle "on" to flip the puckering to other side of the internal line. 2. or right-click on the puckering to apply the options as needed. Menu Description Select All With Same Property Selects puckering with the same styles as the selected puckering. Assign to New Puckering Adds and applies a new puckering style. Delete Deletes the puckering. Note: You can also delete by pressing the Delete key on your keyboard. Puckering Window Open the Puckering window from the window selection menu. In this window, you can create, select, and modify puckering styles. If no settings are made, the "Default_Puckering" style is applied by default. Top menu of the Puckering window Menu Description Add A new style will be added with the same Default Puckering style properties. Note: To create a new puckering style using an existing puckering file, browse to the location where the puckering file is stored in the Library and drag &amp drop the desired puckering style onto the Styles puckering tab. Alternatively, drag &amp drop the puckering file from your OS's file browser. Copy Copies the selected puckering style. Assign Select a puckering object in the 2D window and click 'Apply' to add it as a style with the Default property. Delete Unused Delete unused (not applied to a puckering line) Puckering styles. Note: You can only delete a puckering style if there is no puckering applied to it. Puckering right-click menu Menu Description Delete Deletes the selected Puckering style. Note: You can also delete them with the Delete button on the keyboard. A Puckering Style can only be deleted if there is no Puckering assigned to it. Rename Rename the Puckering style. Reset Resets the properties of the Puckering style to the Default Puckering properties. Copy Copies the selected Puckering style. Merge to New Puckering Combines the selected Puckering styles into a single Puckering. The resulting Puckering style will have the Default Puckering property. Assign Puckering style Applies the Puckering style to the selected Puckering lines. Apply with a generated Puckering style 1. When generating Puckering: After selecting a Puckering style in the Puckering window, it will be applied as the selected style when generated. 2. Apply after Puckering is created: Select a Puckering line and click the 'Apply' button to the right of the Puckering style. Apply as a new Puckering Style 1. select a Puckering line and add it with the 'Assign' button at the top of the Puckering window. 2. Select a Puckering line and add it to the 'Assign to New Puckering' menu from the right-click menu. Puckering Style Properties You can adjust the properties of the Puckering style to achieve different forms of puckering. When you select a Puckering Style in the Puckering window, the Puckering Style properties appear in the Properties window. Open/Save Puckering Styles: You can save and recall styles via the Open and Save buttons at the top of the properties window. Puckering Style Properties Information Name Change the name of the puckering style. Material There are five presets available: Cotton, Denim, Leather, Nylon, and Polyester. Basic Parameters Texture Apply a texture. Desaturation Use to leave the pattern or texture of the texture image and vary the overall color of the rest of the image. Shadow Intensity Adjusts the shadow intensity of the texture. Shadow Brightness Adjusts the brightness of the shadows, leaving the pattern or texture of the texture image. Normal Map Brings up a normal map to change the appearance of the puckering. Intensity (%) Adjusts the intensity. Color Adjusts the colour of the texture. Opacity Adjusts the transparency of the texture. Specification Density % Adjusts the density of the texture. Width Adjusts the width. Show/Hide Puckering You can show or hide the overall puckering. Steps 1. In the 2D window Location Main Menu Display Materials Show Puckerings View icon in 2D window 2D Sewing Show Puckerings 2. In the 3D window Location Main Menu Display Materials Show Puckering View icon in 3D window 3D Trims Display Show Puckering End Result You can show or hide all the created puckering in the window.

Title: Fold/Sew Pleats
Content: Objective Create a variety of pleats, fold and sew them (ver2.3.0). Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Pleats Pleats Fold / Pleats Sewing 2D Toolbar Pleats Fold / Pleats Sewing Operation Pleats Fold Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Pleats Pleats Fold 2D Toolbar Pleats Fold Click to establish the initial point for the direction of the pleats, then double-click to establish the end point. Pleats Fold window appears. Select a desired type of pleats. Depending on the selected pleats type, the Fold Angles of the Internal Lines are now being highlighted. Note: Yellow: Outside fold line (Fold angle of zero(0) degree), Light-blue: Inside fold line (Fold angle of 360 degree), Not highlighted: No fold line (Fold angle of 180 degree) Check Reverse Direction option as needed. The direction of pleats being folded are now being reversed. Click OK button to complete. Pleats Sewing Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Pleats Pleats Sewing 2D Toolbar Pleats Sewing Click on the initial point and drag up to the end point of the seamline on the pleats Pattern. On the pleats Pattern, click on the first Sewing Line to begin with, and move the mouse to the end point. Sewing is now being established for every three(3) segments (the amount of segments needed to create each individual pleat). Click on the end point to complete. The color of the fluorescent sewing lines are now being changed for respective seam color, indicating that the sewing is being completed.

Title: UI Changes (Above ver. 11)
Content: Layout Window [Workspace Windows / Side Windows] Select Mode - Every window can be changed from one to another through the drop-down list at the top center of the window. Duplicate Window - Select a Duplicate icon at the top right-hand corner of a window, and the window will be duplicated as a pop-up. Reset to Default Layout -By toggling the Reset to Default Layout in the bottom right-hand corner, you can bring the window layout back to its original settings. [Workspace Windows] Set up the number of the Workspace Windows - You can set up the window view options at the bottom right-hand corner of the screen. - As many as four Workspace Window can be shown at one time. - With the shortcut 'Alt+W', you can switch between the current window layout and a full screen of the selected window . (ver. 12.1) [Side Windows] Close Windows - Only Side windows can be closed, not the Workspace windows. - Select X at the top right-hand corner to close the window. Show/Hide Window - Only Side windows can be either shown and hidden, not the Workspace windows. - Select the arrow on the top left-hand corner to hide the window. Its title will appear as a tab on either side of the screen after being hidden. - If you click on that tab, the window appears again. Arrange Windows - All pop-up windows can be arranged by dragging on either side of the window. Create Windows Tab - Each pop-up window can be dragged onto an existing side window to group them together. - Their title will appear as tabs at the bottom of the window. - You can select a tab to view each window in a group. Toolbar Arrange Toolbar - You can relocate the toolbar to the top, bottom, left, and right of a window by clicking the control handle on the leftmost side Show/Hide Toolbar - Toggle the Show/Hide Toolbar button at the far right of the view icons in each window to make it appear or disappear. Duplicate Tool Group - Move Mouse over a tool group to find sub-tools of the tool group. - A tool group can be duplicated as a pop-up by either clicking the dashed line with scissors in the tool group or by pressing the Enter key. Modular Editor - Modular Editor is added to the tool bar on the 2D window. - You can use the existing Modular Editor, by toggling the Modular Editor icon. Main Menu Duplicate the Menu list - A dash line will be shown if you click a main menu which can be duplicated as a pop-up. - If you either click the dashed line with scissors in a main menu or press the Enter key, the main menu will be duplicated as a pop-up. Open New Window - Main Menu &gt Display &gt Window - Main Menu &gt Window (ver. 12.1) - Follow the indicated path above to open the desired window as a pop up. Environment The Light, Wind, and Camera Controllers icons have been changed. Note - You can restore UI to default by clicking the bottom right icon

Title: Active Tool Hotkey Reference Window
Content: Objective Show the most important hotkeys for the currently active window or tool. This helps new users become familiar with hotkeys, and exposes hotkeys that do not/cannot have a button in the User Interface. Location Dropdown Window Selection Active Hotkey Viewer Operation In any workspace window, use the drop-down menu to select Active Tool Hotkey Viewer. Select a Tool from the toolbar for either the 2D Pattern Window or 3D Window. Observe that all hotkeys available for the active toolset group are visible in the Active Tool Hotkey Viewer, organized into collapsible sections. Select another tool for use and observe that the Active Tool Hotkey Viewer updates accordingly.

Title: Store (Above ver. 11)
Content: Objective Now you can either purchase or download garment items from the Store within the Marvelous Designer Software. (Windows/MAC) Location Select the Store Tab on the left side of the screen. Operation The Store is only available when signing-in with your account registered on www.marvelousdesigner.com Left click the Sign In icon on the top right hand corner of the screen to login. Menu Description Item List : All items in the store appear. Hover your mouse over an item to see its name and price You can click like icon on any item you like or add it to the cart. Key-in what you want in the search bar at the left top of the screen You can search by entering keywords in the search bar. Use the Filter to view items in a desired category. Items can be sorted in a desired order, using the 'Sort By' drop-down menu at the upper right-hand corner. Turn 'Don't show owned item' on in order not to view what you have already purchased. (Available for those who sign-in.) Detail : See the details of any selected item. Double clicking an item to view the detailed information. The seller name can be found below the name of an item. You can select the license type to purchase, either 'Basic' or 'Extended', and find the description of the license at the bottom. Click the '3D Viewer' button to view the item in 3D. After selecting a license for the item, click the 'Add to Cart' button to add the item to your cart. You can find the tags and descriptions of the item. (Only available when registered by the seller.) Item images edited by the seller are also available. Click the arrow icon on either side of the image, or select the page number at the bottom, to navigate through additional images.. Cart : Check the items added in the Cart and buy them. You can check the total quantity and price of your items, and delete any items you don't want to purchase. Click the 'Checkout' to bring up the purchase page. My Item : Check the items purchased and download them. All items you have purchased appears as a list. Click the 'Download' to download any purchased item.

Title: [Mode] SCULPT
Content: Objective Sculpt garments using various brush tools. (ver. 8) Location SCULPT Mode Brush Tool Operation Select SCULPT mode on the menu select menu at the top right of Marvelous Designer. The Brush toolbar appears in the upper left corner of the SCULPT mode screen. Select a Brush tool from Brush toolbar. When mouseover on 3D garment after selecting a brush tool, can check brush Size and Focal setting. With a brush is selected, brush property will be displayed. Adjust Strenght, Size, Focal, Spacing Depth on Brush property. Also can change brush type and property setting on 3D window pop up menu (shortcut:B). Click and drag on 3D garment to sculpt. Press the Shift key on the keyboard while using any type of Brush tool. 3D garment will be displayed with gray in SCULPT mode. Adjust the color either material of 3D garment on Material Type on the property window. Brush Types Wrinkle Left-click and drag to create wrinkles on the brush area. (ver. 10) Release Left-click + Shift and drag to release wrinkles on brush area. (ver. 10) Sculpt Emboss mesh. With invert option activated, engraves mesh. Smooth Makes the surface flat on average. (Shortcut: Shift) Grab Moves vertexes to express pulled surface. Stamp Use an image as a stamp. Pinch Close the position of the vertexes, makes the surface sharper. Brush Property Depending on the type of brush, the properties you apply vary. Brush Property Description Brush Type Wrinkle Release Sculpt Smooth Grab Stamp Pinch Simulation Preset Simulation types that are applied when using Wrinkle and Release brush (ver. 10) O O X X X X X Strength Strength of brush. X X O O O O O Size Size of brush. O O O O O O O Focal Coverage of brush. (similar with Hardness) O O O O O O O Spacing Interval of brush. X X O X X X X Depth Depth of brush. X X O O O X O Invert Change the direction of a brush. (shortcut: Alt) X X O X X O X Image Using an image as brush. X X O X O O X Realistic Realistic (ver. 10) (Setting for Wrinkle, Release brush) O O X X X X X Layer Layer (ver. 10) (Setting for Wrinkle, Release brush) O O X X X X X Using an image as brush Click button next to Image. Click an Image from default images. - Focal setting is not available for image brush. Click &amp Drag on 3D garment to Sculpt. - Click &amp Drag to adjust the size and angle for Stamp brush. To turn off an image, click button and select Off. - Focal setting appears on brush property after turning off image. Adding image Click + button next to image. Select an image on the file browser. Click &amp Drag on 3D garment to Sculpt. - Click &amp Drag to adjust the size and angle for Stamp brush. After adding image, can load the image by clicking button next to the image. Creating image Image file should be Black and white (mono-tone). White area emboss when using it as a brush. Double Side Display With Double Side option activated, can check both back and front side of mesh. Show/Hide 3D Pattern (Shortcut Shift+Q) Show selected pattern only - Select a pattern while input Shift+Q, other patterns will be hidden. Reverse selected pattern/hidden pattern - After operating no.1 above, click on the selected pattern while input Shift+Q to reverse hidden pattern/ selected pattern. Adding hidden patterns - To hide additional patterns, click on a pattern which you want to hide while input Shift+Q. Show All 3D Patterns - Click on the background while input Shift+Q to show all pattern. 3D Garment Rendering Style You can set the following menus from the View Settings icon on the left of the 3D window. Show Internal Lines Monochrome Surface (Alt+3) / Wireframe on Surface (Alt+6)
